'''RED Canids''' is a Brazilian team, created with the acquisition of [[INTZ Red]]. During the first split of 2018, the team competed under the name '''Red Canids Corinthians''', as a result of a partnership with sports club [[Corinthians Esports|SC Corinthians Paulista]]. Currently the team competes as '''RED Canids Kalunga''', as part of a title sponsorship deal with Brazilian stationery store [https://www.kalunga.com.br/ Kalunga].

== History ==
=== 2015/2016 ===
In December 2015, it was announced that [[INTZ Red|INTZ RED]] was acquired by a "group of investors", and renamed to '''RED Canids'''. After some news revealed that the team's owners were still related to INTZ, Riot ordered the INTZ organization to sell/transfer one of the teams, or it would lose its {{bl|CBLOL 2016 Split 1}} spot. Finally, before the start of the tournament, INTZ sold RED Canids to '''Brasil Mega Arena''' owner {{bl|Fekz|Felippe Corradini}}. The team finished the [[CBLOL 2016 Split 1|regular season]] in sixth place, with a score of 8 points, 2 wins, 2 ties and 3⁠ losses. In [[CBLOL 2016 Split 1|playoffs]], after losing to [[Operation Kino e-Sports]] and defeating [[paiN Gaming]], they ended up in 5th place. 
For the [[CBLOL 2016 Split 2|second split]], they decided to bring in [[Eryon]], who would compete for the starting toplaner position with [[Ayel]]. Despite the change, they ended up in seventh place, barely making it to the playoffs. For the [[CBLOL 2016 Split 2 Playoffs|playoffs]], they brought in Estonian toplaner [[beansu]]. The team ended up taking seventh place in the playoffs after winning the '''Relegation''' match against [[Big Gods]], who was demoted to the [[BRCC 2017 Split 1]].

=== 2017 ===
For [[CBLOL 2017 Split 1|2017]], RED Canids brought the lineup known as the "renegades": bringing [[Robo]], [[Nappon]], [[tockers]], [[brTT]], players who ended up leaving their teams after being replaced, and keeping [[Dioud]], a player who remained from the previous lineup. They finished the first split in second place, only behind [[INTZ]], with 16 points, 5 wins, 1 tie and 1 loss. With the return of [[YoDa (Felipe Noronha)|YoDa]] as a alternating midlaner with [[tockers]] and [[Sacy]] as a substitute for [[brTT]], they won their first title in 2017 after beating [[Keyd Stars]] in the finals by 3-0 and participated in [[MSI 2017]], which was held in Brazil. With the help of [[Brokenshard]] as a temporary coach, they ended up second place in group stage, with a record of 4 wins and 2 loses, but not qualifying for the main stage.
In [[CBLOL 2017 Split 2|2017's second split]], they brough the Portuguese [[Rhuckz]] as a substitute support for [[Dioud]] and [[Galfi]] as the new head coach for the team, finishing second place in regular season, but losing to [[Team oNe eSports]] by 3-2 in the [[CBLOL 2017 Split 2 Playoffs|playoffs]].

=== 2018 ===
At the end of 2017, the team announced the departure of several players, such as [[Rhuckz]], [[tockers]], [[Robo]] and [[brTT]]. The surprise came with the announcement that two Korean players were joining the team, the jungler [[Winged]] and the midlaner [[Sky (Kim Ha-neul)|Sky]], in addition to the remaining of the jungler [[Nappon]] and botlaner [[Sacy]], the joining of support [[Cabu]] and their new coach [[Icarus (Lee In-cheol)|Icarus]]. They finished second in [[CBLOL 2018 Split 1|regular season]], but they ended up losing to [[Keyd Stars]] by 3-2 and finishing third place in the [[CBLOL 2018 Split 1 Playoffs|playoffs]].
The [[CBLOL 2018 Split 2|second split of 2018]] is often regarded as the lowest point in the team's history after [[Dioud]] and [[Nappon]] left and they hired the korean jungler [[Chaser]] to replace [[Winged]]. The team also rehired the coach [[Abaxial]], who was part of the team two years before, and hired [[Coelho]], a coach considered a newcomer to the scene. They ended up eight place, which ended up demoting the team to the [[Brazilian Challenger Circuit/2019 Season/Split 1|Challenged Circuit]].

=== 2019 ===
With their demotion to the [[Brazilian Challenger Circuit/2019 Season/Split 1|Challenger Circuit]], the team decided to bet on new and old players, bringing in rookies [[Guigo]] and [[Avenger (Adriano Perassoli)|Avenger]], their old acquaintance [[YoDa (Felipe Noronha)|YoDa]] and the veteran [[Revolta]], which were led by the Canadian coach [[Nuddle]] after [[Coelho]] was moved to their [[RED Academy|academy team]]. They finished first place in the regular season, but finished third place after losing to [[Team oNe eSports]] by 3-1 in the [[Brazilian Challenger Circuit/2019 Season/Split 1 Playoffs|playoffs]], who was also demoted in the previous year.
For the [[Brazilian Challenger Circuit/2019 Season/Split 2|second split]], the team welcomed [[TitaN]], the botlaner from [[KaBuM! Esports]] who had already won 2 CBLOL titles and 1 BRCC with the orange team. Despite the player's entry, the team finished second in the regular phase and third in the [[Brazilian Challenger Circuit/2019 Season/Split 2 Playoffs|playoffs]], losing 3-0 to [[ProGaming Esports]].

=== 2020 ===
For [[Brazilian Challenger Circuit/2020 Season/Split 1|2020]], the team decided to aim higher, bringing in former teammate [[Ayel]], as well as rookies [[Aegis (Gabriel Lemos)|Aegis]], [[Grevthar]] and [[Woodboy]]. The gamble was a risky one, and by finishing fifth, they almost lost their spot in the Challenger Circuit. The second split of [[Brazilian Challenger Circuit/2020 Season/Split 2|2020]] would be seen as one of the most importants of the team. With the toplaner [[Guigo]] and the support [[Cabu]] moving into the starting lineup, they finished first place in the regular season and won the [[Brazilian Challenger Circuit/2020 Season/Split 2 Playoffs|playoffs]] by defeating [[Team oNe eSports]] by 3-1, promoting them to the [[CBLOL 2021 Split 1]], unknown to them that their would be chosen for the new franchise format of [[CBLOL]] anyway. The team also participated in late 2020 in the only edition of the [[Liga Loading de Esports 2020|LLE 2020]], promoted by a television channel, in which they won R$ 50.000 after defeating [[Vorax]] in the grand finals by 3-0.

=== 2021 ===
The first split of the new [[CBLOL 2021 Split 1|CBLOL]] had good results with the entrance of the new support, [[JoJo (Gabriel Dzelme)|JoJo]], and the team finished third place in the regular season. Despite a good start in the [[CBLOL 2021 Split 1 Playoffs|playoffs]] with a win by 3-1 against [[KaBuM! Esports]], the team lost to [[Vorax]] by 3-1 and finished fourth place. The [[CBLOL 2021 Split 2|second split]] had worst results, finishing in sixth place and almost not qualifying for [[CBLOL 2021 Split 2 Playoffs|playoffs]]. With the entrance of [[Grevthar]], who was moved to the academy team in the previous split, the team made a miracle run and won the title, qualifying for [[Worlds 2021]]. 
In [[Worlds 2021]], the team started the '''Play-in Stage''' in group A facing and defeating the Costa Rican [[INFINITY]]. They afterwards faced the asian teams [[LNG Esports]] and [[Hanwha Life Esports]], losing to both of them. They also faced the Australian team [[PEACE (Oceanic Team)|PEACE]], who eventually defeated them both in the groups stage and in the tierbreakers, eliminating the team.
